source.title: Class Interference of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Dong-Cui Diao; Heng-Shuai Yao; Bei Jiang

record.tranche_reason: Measures natural-label test performance across architectures and learning-rate setups and relates class-wise test errors to loss sensitivity, using measures different from the claim versions' specified tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label test accuracies and class-wise errors, but does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolution versus fully connected networks, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Cited results about other studies are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures class confusion, learning-rate effects and loss sensitivity along class-gradient directions. None tests V1–V8. Its sharpness visualizations do not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps; batch-size findings are cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors describe class interference as a classification bottleneck reflecting data difficulty and propose cross-class tests, class-gradient loss visualizations and label-dancing diagnostics to study it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 class-wise test errors and class-gradient loss visualizations; it does not reproduce the listed version-specific methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies across the three learning-rate setups; class-wise recall and reported interference vary by class and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger fixed learning rates and cosine annealing improve CIFAR-10 test accuracy for VGG19 and ResNet18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these models and training recipes, test accuracy depends on learning-rate magnitude and scheduling.

fits_no_version.finding: CAT and DOG have comparatively low recall across the tested convolutional classifiers; the authors identify mutual confusion as a major source of errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-specific confusion reveals uneven classification difficulty that overall test accuracy obscures.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3 reports direction-dependent loss sharpness. Small-learning-rate ResNet18 appears sharper than VGG19 while achieving 86.88% versus 84.99% test accuracy; annealed models have broad flat regions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness visualized along class-gradient directions depends on direction and learning-rate setup and need not order test accuracy across architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: Submitted to ICLR 2023 for review; venue otherwise stated as arXiv.org
record.problems: The reported test-accuracy table gives no uncertainty estimates or corresponding training accuracy. Loss visualizations are described qualitatively; their plotted values are not extracted as rows.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible numerical results were omitted. Figure-only loss-landscape and cross-class matrix results are described in the text but do not report extractable values for the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance, paired with natural-label training under the same recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons, training-set-size dependence and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps within one convolutional family at similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing high-memorization examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The recorded numerical values match the supplied text. States are changed to cannot_determine because none of these measures establishes a listed version; this does not dispute the reported accuracies. No version-specific results require additional rows.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-scaled perturbation measure or comparison of gap rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
